standard_prerequisites.name: Dimension is invariant under etale morphisms, and for a quasi-separated decent space it equals the Krull dimension
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Properties of Spaces, label spaces-properties-lemma-dimension-decent-invariant-under-etale (invoked at proof line 1785) and Decent Spaces, label decent-spaces-lemma-dimension-decent-space (invoked at proof line 1789)
standard_prerequisites.use: They let the argument work with honest Krull dimension on the auxiliary schemes that appear, everything etale over $X$ having dimension at most $d$.

standard_prerequisites.name: Etale cohomology of a quasi-coherent module on a scheme agrees with usual cohomology, also with support in a closed subscheme
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Descent, label descent-proposition-same-cohomology-quasi-coherent (invoked at proof line 1795) and Etale Cohomology, label etale-cohomology-lemma-cohomology-with-support-quasi-coherent (invoked at proof line 1798)
standard_prerequisites.use: They identify the cohomology computed on the auxiliary schemes $V_p$ with the usual sheaf cohomology, where the vanishing statement for schemes applies.

standard_prerequisites.name: Filtration of a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space by open pieces with etale schemes over them
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Decent Spaces, label decent-spaces-lemma-filter-quasi-compact-quasi-separated (invoked at proof line 1803)
standard_prerequisites.use: It provides the chain $\emptyset = U_{n+1} \subset U_n \subset \ldots \subset U_1 = X$ and the quasi-compact separated schemes $V_p \to U_p$ which are surjective etale and isomorphisms over $T_p = U_p \setminus U_{p+1}$.

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of cohomology above the cohomological dimension of a scheme
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology, label cohomology-proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral (invoked at proof lines 1818 and 1831)
standard_prerequisites.use: It gives the vanishing over the auxiliary schemes $V_p$, which is transported back along the filtration pieces.

standard_prerequisites.name: Localization of cohomology with support along an etale morphism that is an isomorphism over the support
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-etale-localization-sheaf-with-support (invoked at proof lines 1828 and 1839)
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the cohomology with support $H^q_{T_p}(U_p, \mathcal{F})$ into cohomology with support on the scheme $V_p$, where vanishing is known.

core_obligations: Collect the preliminary facts: dimension at most $d$ is inherited by every space etale over $X$, on quasi-separated spaces it is the Krull dimension, and on schemes etale cohomology (with support) agrees with usual cohomology (proof lines 1784-1799).
Use the filtration by open pieces and the auxiliary etale schemes $V_p \to U_p$ which are isomorphisms over $T_p$ (proof lines 1801-1812).

Prove (1) by induction downwards along the filtration: the bottom piece $U_n = V_n$ is a scheme, so cohomology vanishes above $d$; if the vanishing is known on $U_{p+1}$, then it suffices to know $H^q_{T_p}(U_p, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for $q > d$, and that group equals $H^q_{f_p^{-1}(T_p)}(V_p, \mathcal{F})$ by etale localization of cohomology with support, which vanishes on the scheme $V_p$ (proof lines 1814-1832).

Prove (2) for a quasi-compact open $U$: enlarge to $U' = U \cup U_n$ and use that $H^q_Z(U', \mathcal{F}) = H^q_Z(U_n, \mathcal{F})$ for $Z = U' \setminus U$ vanishes above $d$ on the scheme $U_n$, giving surjectivity of $H^d(U', \mathcal{F}) \to H^d(U, \mathcal{F})$; then repeat the same argument with $U' = U \cup U_p$ and the morphism $f_p$ until $U$ contains $U_1 = X$ (proof lines 1834-1858).
Record that (2) formally implies the vanishing with support in (3) (proof lines 1860-1861).
proof_roadmap: Preliminaries on dimension and on etale versus usual cohomology (proof lines 1784-1799).
The filtration and the auxiliary etale schemes $V_p$ (proof lines 1801-1812).
Vanishing above the dimension by downwards induction (proof lines 1814-1832).
Surjectivity in the top degree by enlarging the open (proof lines 1834-1858).
Part (3) as a formal consequence of (2) (proof lines 1860-1861).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the dimension bound for the cohomology of a quasi-coherent module on a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space, together with the surjectivity of the restriction map in the top degree and vanishing with support (statement lines 1769-1781). The proof filters the space into open pieces dominated by quasi-compact separated schemes that are etale and isomorphisms over the successive differences, transfers cohomology with support along these covers, and runs a downwards induction that uses the vanishing theorem for schemes as its input; the top degree statement is proved by the same enlargement procedure. The filtration and the transport of cohomology with support are the substance, so the claim is H2.
